I've handled the S-105 delay. Only one product is hit: Lacrivia 0.1% 10 mL. It is short at one warehouse (DC-EAST), and I split that stock among customers. No purchase order went to the backup supplier because it is on a quality hold. I notified all 23 affected accounts and asked Trade Relations to tell the two DC-EAST wholesalers.

I followed the standard process for this kind of disruption (Supply Disruption Response). No proven playbook matched this case, but the process covered it, so I didn't use the exploratory mode that flags a run for human review.

**What I found**
- **The late order:** S-105 (Everline Packaging) has open order PO000869 for 5,800 units of CMP-502, a 10 mL dropper bottle. It was due to ship 2026-10-04 and now ships around 2026-10-25.
- **Product affected:** CMP-502 goes into one finished product: Lacrivia 0.1% 10 mL (FG-1002, NDC 99101-0101-10), made at plant PL-01.
- **Backup supplier:** S-108 (Halvorsen Closures) is qualified and approved to ship to PL-01, but the supplier portal shows it on quality hold (closure torque failures, corrective action open). So no available supplier can cover the gap.
- **Recovery date:** About 2026-11-19 at the warehouses. After the bottles arrive, it takes 25 days: 3 days transit, 3 days fill and QC, 14 days for the sterility test and release, 4 days to the warehouse.
- **Stock against safety levels (2026-09-25 count):**

| Warehouse | On hand | Safety stock | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| DC-EAST | 34 | 233 | Below — about 2 days of supply |
| DC-CENTRAL | 351 | 155 | Above — about 30 days |
| DC-WEST | 324 | 129 | Above — about 34 days |

- **Substitute:** The other Lacrivia pack (5 mL) can't be offered because it is also below safety stock at DC-EAST (46 vs 471). The approved substitute, Cyclosporine OS 0.05% 5 mL, is not made with CMP-502 and is well stocked at DC-EAST (615 vs 252), so that is what account teams were told to offer.

**What I did**
1. **Split the DC-EAST stock (plan AL-BA541D8D):** All 34 units go to the three Tier A health systems, in proportion to their last-13-week prescriptions (TRx) of this pack in the states DC-EAST serves. Leftover units after rounding went to the largest account.
   - Riverbend (AC00059): 15 units (271 prescriptions)
   - Oak Hollow (AC00038): 11 units (237)
   - Northfield (AC00117): 8 units (174)
   - Tier B and all other accounts get nothing; the Tier A demand used up all 34 units.
   - The plan is worth $26,520 at the $780 list price. That is under the $50,000 approval limit and moves no stock between warehouses, so no approval was needed.
2. **Notified account teams (23 tasks, one per DC-EAST account with prescriptions of this pack).** Each message gives the account's units (or none), the ~2026-11-19 recovery date and the Cyclosporine OS substitute.
   - Tier A: CRM-9F61F5EB (AC00059), CRM-008F1E4F (AC00038), CRM-30F0C469 (AC00117).
   - Tier B: CRM-0D18061D (AC00001), CRM-CC05F8DD (AC00138).
   - All other accounts: CRM-1B17DD9F, CRM-85C5E6DF, CRM-20FB445A, CRM-4D94175C, CRM-22917AB3, CRM-AD030BEF, CRM-5EF711C2, CRM-46DDE0D8, CRM-73FD4045, CRM-DE3B7D34, CRM-CF89367A, CRM-8DD54EC7, CRM-A8DF21C4, CRM-FC422EC1, CRM-E497CA0D, CRM-D2DEF0B3, CRM-EB1AEA89, CRM-D7FF3180.
3. **Wholesaler notice (CASE-A2C587A6, owner Trade Relations):** The system for sending notices to wholesalers has no connection I can use, so I asked Trade Relations to notify W-01 Keystone Drug Distributors and W-02 Atlas Pharma Supply, the two wholesalers DC-EAST serves.

- **No order to S-108:** It is on quality hold.
- **No split at DC-CENTRAL or DC-WEST:** Both are above safety stock, and the rules only allow splitting stock where it is below.
- **No transfer to DC-EAST from another warehouse:** It would need Supply Planning lead approval. All warehouses depend on the same delayed plant, so moving stock would only shift the shortage. The lead can still ask for one.
- **No wholesaler stock check:** The wholesaler inventory feed returned an error (HTTP 503, not loaded yet).
- **No patient-level data used, per data-use policy POL-DUA-01.**

I followed the standard process for this kind of disruption (Supply Disruption Response). No proven playbook matched this case, but the process covered it, so I didn't use the exploratory mode that flags a run for human review.

**What I found**
- **The late order:** S-105 (Everline Packaging) has open order PO000869 for 5,800 units of CMP-502, a 10 mL dropper bottle. It was due to ship 2026-10-04 and now ships around 2026-10-25.
- **Product affected:** CMP-502 goes into one finished product: Lacrivia 0.1% 10 mL (FG-1002, NDC 99101-0101-10), made at plant PL-01.
- **Backup supplier:** S-108 (Halvorsen Closures) is qualified and approved to ship to PL-01, but the supplier portal shows it on quality hold (closure torque failures, corrective action open). So no available supplier can cover the gap.
- **Recovery date:** About 2026-11-19 at the warehouses. After the bottles arrive, it takes 25 days: 3 days transit, 3 days fill and QC, 14 days for the sterility test and release, 4 days to the warehouse.
- **Stock against safety levels (2026-09-25 count):**

| Warehouse | On hand | Safety stock | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| DC-EAST | 34 | 233 | Below — about 2 days of supply |
| DC-CENTRAL | 351 | 155 | Above — about 30 days |
| DC-WEST | 324 | 129 | Above — about 34 days |

- **Substitute:** The other Lacrivia pack (5 mL) can't be offered because it is also below safety stock at DC-EAST (46 vs 471). The approved substitute, Cyclosporine OS 0.05% 5 mL, is not made with CMP-502 and is well stocked at DC-EAST (615 vs 252), so that is what account teams were told to offer.

**What I did**
1. **Split the DC-EAST stock (plan AL-BA541D8D):** All 34 units go to the three Tier A health systems, in proportion to their last-13-week prescriptions (TRx) of this pack in the states DC-EAST serves. Leftover units after rounding went to the largest account.
   - Riverbend (AC00059): 15 units (271 prescriptions)
   - Oak Hollow (AC00038): 11 units (237)
   - Northfield (AC00117): 8 units (174)
   - Tier B and all other accounts get nothing; the Tier A demand used up all 34 units.
   - The plan is worth $26,520 at the $780 list price. That is under the $50,000 approval limit and moves no stock between warehouses, so no approval was needed.
2. **Notified account teams (23 tasks, one per DC-EAST account with prescriptions of this pack).** Each message gives the account's units (or none), the ~2026-11-19 recovery date and the Cyclosporine OS substitute.
   - Tier A: CRM-9F61F5EB (AC00059), CRM-008F1E4F (AC00038), CRM-30F0C469 (AC00117).
   - Tier B: CRM-0D18061D (AC00001), CRM-CC05F8DD (AC00138).
   - All other accounts: CRM-1B17DD9F, CRM-85C5E6DF, CRM-20FB445A, CRM-4D94175C, CRM-22917AB3, CRM-AD030BEF, CRM-5EF711C2, CRM-46DDE0D8, CRM-73FD4045, CRM-DE3B7D34, CRM-CF89367A, CRM-8DD54EC7, CRM-A8DF21C4, CRM-FC422EC1, CRM-E497CA0D, CRM-D2DEF0B3, CRM-EB1AEA89, CRM-D7FF3180.
3. **Wholesaler notice (CASE-A2C587A6, owner Trade Relations):** The system for sending notices to wholesalers has no connection I can use, so I asked Trade Relations to notify W-01 Keystone Drug Distributors and W-02 Atlas Pharma Supply, the two wholesalers DC-EAST serves.

**What I did not do, and why**
- **No order to S-108:** It is on quality hold.
- **No split at DC-CENTRAL or DC-WEST:** Both are above safety stock, and the rules only allow splitting stock where it is below.
- **No transfer to DC-EAST from another warehouse:** It would need Supply Planning lead approval. All warehouses depend on the same delayed plant, so moving stock would only shift the shortage. The lead can still ask for one.
- **No wholesaler stock check:** The wholesaler inventory feed returned an error (HTTP 503, not loaded yet).
- **No patient-level data used, per data-use policy POL-DUA-01.**

**Assumptions and risks**
- I assumed only PO000869 slips. If S-105's later orders (PO000870–872) slip too, DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST run out around 2026-10-25 and 2026-10-29, before supply recovers. I'd re-check them at the next weekly stock count.
- S-108's open order PO000887 (4,900 units, due 2026-10-18) is probably blocked by its quality hold too. I counted no supply from it.
- To place prescriptions in DC-EAST's states I used the state of each prescriber's clinic, and I rolled clinics up to their top-level health system.
- Independent clinics with names like "Sunridge Vision Associates 20" have no parent health system in the account data, so they don't get that system's contract tier.

**Knowledge-layer sources used:** process Supply Disruption Response (SDR-1.1 to 4.2); rules BR-ALLOC-01/02, BR-APPR-01, BR-SUB-01/02, BR-LEAD-01, BR-CUST-01, BR-REGION-01; reference sets supply_contracts, list_prices, dc_service_regions, approved_substitutes and ndc_crosswalk; the supply-exposure trace and lead-time lookup.
